determinism_note: Determinism scope. Same-seed greedy decoding produces identical token sequences on CPU at a fixed thread count AND a fixed batch size, with the torch version and BLAS backend recorded in this manifest. Batch size is load-bearing here: padding a batch changes floating-point reduction order, so the same prompt run alone and run inside a batch may diverge -- the batch size used is recorded in this manifest's inference block. Log-probabilities match to a documented tolerance rather than bit-exactly. On GPU the guarantee is metric-level only, within a reported tolerance: kernel selection, atomic reduction order, and cuBLAS workspace reuse are not fully controllable. Changing thread count, batch size, BLAS backend, torch version, or hardware invalidates bit-level comparison. No unconditional bit-identity is claimed.

metrics.coding: sum_to_zero (deviation) contrasts; every level's coefficient emitted
metrics.cov_type: cluster-robust, clustered by item (prompt); statsmodels cov_type='cluster'
metrics.harm_series: equal-weight mean of the harm type's scorers' standardized scores
metrics.model_formula: harm_std ~ A + B + A:B, over an axis pair's order-2 cells
metrics.resampling_unit: item (prompt), resampled with replacement within each cell; percentile interval
